note: Passage 3702 (Pro 1:4) — prudence/knowledge/discretion given to the simple and the youth. 'simple' (peti) read as the naive inner STATE the book targets; discretion (mezimmah) here in its positive sense.

dims.v: the simple — the naive, untaught, morally open inner condition
the simple/naive person the book addresses
the naive inner state that stands open, needing prudence put into it
paired with the youth (naar) as the un-formed recipients
peti is not an act but a CONDITION — the open, gullible inner state; the book exists to give it prudence (ormah). Read as a characteristic-state, the starting point the whole book works on.
knowledge given to fill the naive inner life
paired with discretion (mezimmah) as the gift to the youth
daat here is the content given, opposite of the simple's emptiness; distinct from binah (discernment) and chokmah (competence).
discretion — shrewd forethought (here the positive sense)
shrewd forethought put into the young inner life
paired with knowledge as the gift to the youth

mezimmah is BIVALENT — 'scheming' in the wicked (its usual Proverbs edge, the seed's 'IB:plot' tag) but here POSITIVE: the shrewd forethought given to the youth. The read records the good sense the context forces, noting the dark potential.
